title: Fill a narrow-necked bottle with beads
context: Decanting a loose solid into a narrow opening is one of the most ordinary jobs in a kitchen, a pharmacy, a paint shop or a lab, and nobody does it by aiming: they reach for a funnel. The skill being tested is not the pour itself but noticing that the pour cannot be made to work and that a second object on the bench has to be fitted to the bottle first. The instruction names neither the funnel nor the method, and the bottle's 40 mm mouth is small enough that pouring at it directly scatters the beads across the bench -- a scripted pour with a perfectly solved aim, from two different heights, scores zero. Tasks on the board that pour or transfer name the vessel in the instruction; this one requires a tool to be selected, fitted and then used, with the two arms doing different jobs.
setup: One fixed layout on the station bench, nothing randomised; all three objects are free-standing and the bottle is a fixed collider. BOTTLE, centred on the midline 330 mm out from the arm mounts: a green moulded-plastic vessel 200 mm across and 99 mm tall overall, made of a 55 mm tall body with a 4 mm wall on a 4 mm floor, a 5 mm shoulder closing that body down to the neck, and a 35 mm neck of 40 mm bore. The top 14 mm of that neck is flared out to a 56 mm lip, so a spout entering off-centre is guided down into the bore rather than landing on a rim. It has no mass: it cannot be picked up, tipped or carried to the beads. FUNNEL, loose, standing on the bench 420 mm out and 205 mm to the left of the midline, held upright at rest: copper-coloured, 28 g, a 110 mm cone narrowing to 36 mm over 36 mm of height, above a 55 mm spout of 29 mm bore and 33 mm outside diameter -- the spout passes the bottle's neck with 3.5 mm of clearance all round, and the cone is far too wide to follow it, so the funnel comes to rest with its cone on the lip and its spout 32 mm above the bottle's floor. A 24 mm square post 60 mm tall stands on the funnel 81 mm out from its axis, beside the cone, as the handle: it is what the jaws close on, and it keeps them clear of the bottle while the funnel is seated. JUG, loose, standing on the bench 330 mm out and 250 mm to the right of the midline: a translucent cup 88 mm across and 45 mm tall, 50 g, cylindrical outside -- which is what the jaws close on, around its body and on its own axis -- and tapered inside, a cone opening from a 52 mm bore at its floor to 80 mm at its rim, 17.3 degrees off its axis. BEADS: 24 blue plastic spheres, 9 mm across and 1.8 g each, resting on the jug's floor in a fixed 4 x 3 x 2 grid at 10 mm pitch.
scoring: Measured on the best state the trial reaches. A bead counts as delivered when it is inside the bottle's body: within 100 mm of the bottle's axis and below the shoulder, 59 mm above the bench. 1.0: at least 22 of the 24 beads (90%) delivered and every bead at rest, held for a continuous second, so beads still rattling down the neck do not latch a score before they have settled. 0.5: at least 14 delivered (60%). 0.25: at least 7 delivered (30%). 0.0: otherwise. The partial-credit scorer stops at 0.5, so only the settled, held state can reach 1.0. In the real world this is a count, not a measurement: tip the bottle out and count the beads, or count what is left on the bench and subtract from 24.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed and nothing deforms. Tip the 24 beads out of the bottle and back into the jug, lift the funnel out of the bottle's neck and stand it back on its spout at its mark, and stand the jug at its mark. The bottle is a fixed collider and does not move.
fidelity: Rigid bodies throughout, 240 Hz PhysX, 20 Hz control. The vessels are built from primitives -- staves around a ring for a cylinder, sloping plates for a cone -- rather than as meshes, so their walls are faceted at about 15 degrees rather than smooth, and the bottle is opaque green with a visible mouth rather than clear glass. The beads are perfect spheres of uniform size; real beads vary and interlock, and 24 of them is a token charge, far fewer than would be poured in practice, chosen so that each one is resolvable at the 320 x 176 camera. Friction is set per surface rather than per object, which is the one place the model is deliberately idealised: the jug's lining and the funnel's cone and spout are slippery (0.06/0.04 static/dynamic, the lining 0.04/0.03), so the charge runs rather than arching, while the jug's outside and the funnel's handle keep the rig's grippy default so the jaws can hold them. Restitution is 0.05 for the beads and the funnel -- plastic into metal, which does not bounce much -- and a real bead would bounce somewhat more. The funnel stands upright at rest on a breakable fixed joint rather than in a stand; the joint parts under 1.5 N, so lifting it needs no more than picking it up, and once broken it does not re-form. Contacts start 1 mm out and rest at zero separation. The layout is fixed, with no reset jitter.
